title: 30 KB Photo Size: Resize Image to 30 KB | SahiSize
description: Get the 30 KB photo size for signature caps above 20 KB. Your image becomes a 27–30 KB JPG on your own phone. Free, quick and never uploaded.
h1: 30 KB photo size: resize image to 30 KB
intro: The 30 KB photo size covers signature caps that sit above the banking 20 KB. Add your image and get a JPG of 27–30 KB, made on your phone without uploading anything.

steps.name: Add your image
steps.text: Take a photo or pick one from your gallery. JPG, PNG, WebP and iPhone HEIC files all work.

steps.name: Check the target
steps.text: 30 KB is already selected. Type a minimum if your form sets one, and decide whether the pixel size may change.

steps.name: Let it work
steps.text: The tool tries the highest JPEG quality that stays under 30 KB and makes the picture smaller only when it has to.

steps.name: Download
steps.text: When every line of the pass check has a tick, save the JPG and upload it to your form.

faq.q: Is 30 KB enough for a photo?
faq.a: Usually yes for a passport-style photo of about 300×400 px. If your form allows 50 KB, the 50 KB page keeps more detail.

faq.q: What if my form says 10–30 KB?
faq.a: Use this page. The output lands at 27–30 KB, comfortably inside the range.

faq.q: Why is my 30 KB file only 27 or 28 KB?
faq.a: The tool finds the highest quality under the cap and stops there. Anything from 27 to 30 KB passes a 30 KB maximum, and staying slightly under protects you from portals that count 1 KB as 1000 bytes.

sections.h2: Forms that want you to resize an image to 30 KB
paras: UPPSC PCS (and its OTR) caps the signature at 30 KB, at 472×236 px. CTET also lets the signature go up to 30 KB, with a very low 3 KB floor. Watch the minimums on other forms: India Post GDS wants its photo at 30–100 KB and the RRB signature must be 30–49 KB, so a file of 27–30 KB would be too small for both. Use the 50 KB page for GDS and the 45 KB page for RRB.

sections.h2: Quality of a 30 KB photo size JPG
paras: You get enough room for a clear thumb print, or a signature a few hundred pixels across with clean edges and no visible blocks. As a photo compressor setting, 30 KB keeps a passport-style face sharp at normal viewing size.

As a rough guide, a passport-style photo on a plain background stays clean at about 210×280 pixels in 30 KB. A busy background or a dim, noisy shot needs more kilobytes for the same size, and a signature on white paper needs far fewer.

Whatever you add, the download is a baseline JPG (not progressive) between 27 and 30 KB. It stays under 30,000 bytes, so it passes whether the portal counts 1 KB as 1000 or 1024 bytes, and hidden camera and location data are removed.
For a signature, sign with a dark pen on plain white paper and photograph it in daylight. Dark, high-contrast ink compresses far better than faint ink.
Pick the size just under the limit printed on your form. If the form gives both a minimum and a maximum, a range page fills in the minimum for you.
